title: Low-Cost Deployable Seafloor Metal Detection Sensor for Ocean Resource Exploration
department: National Centre for Polar andOcean Research (NCPOR)
description: Design and develop a low-cost deployable ocean-bottom sensor that can be released from a research vessel during surveys to detect and map metal-rich seabed deposits, including polymetallic nodules, hydrothermal sulphides, cobalt-rich crusts and rare-earth-element-bearing sediments, providing a rapid and cost-effective tool for deep-ocean mineral exploration.
summary: Innovation (2/5): draws on standard software/hardware techniques applied to a smart resource conservation problem, placing it in the incremental band. Feasibility (4/5): as a hardware build with moderate integration complexity, a working prototype is realistic in a 36-hour window. Impact (2/5): addresses a more targeted user group within Smart Resource Conservation. Tech Depth (2/5): centers on sensor. Sustainability (4/5): has a clear long-term maintenance path. Scalability (1/5): currently scoped narrowly and would need rework to scale. Total 15/30 -> Red verdict.

detail.title: Low-Cost Deployable Seafloor Metal Detection Sensor for Ocean Resource Exploration

overview.in_plain_terms: Build an affordable sensor that can be dropped from a research vessel to detect metal-rich deposits on the seafloor, like polymetallic nodules and rare-earth sediments, without needing expensive deep-ocean exploration equipment.
overview.why_it_matters: Deep-ocean mineral exploration currently needs expensive equipment. A low-cost deployable sensor could genuinely democratize and speed up this kind of resource mapping.
pain_points: Deep-ocean mineral exploration currently relies on expensive, specialized equipment.
No low-cost, rapidly deployable option exists for preliminary seabed metal-deposit screening.
Mapping metal-rich deposits (nodules, sulphides, crusts, rare-earth sediments) at scale is slow and costly.
overview.background: Deep-ocean mineral resources (polymetallic nodules, hydrothermal sulphides, cobalt-rich crusts, rare-earth-bearing sediments) are valuable but expensive to explore for, motivating a low-cost, rapidly deployable detection alternative.
overview.whats_being_asked: A low-cost, deployable ocean-bottom sensor released from a research vessel to detect and map metal-rich seabed deposits.
expected_solution: Deployable sensor hardware for seabed metal detection.
Detection capability across multiple deposit types (nodules, sulphides, crusts, sediments).
Low-cost design suitable for rapid, repeated deployment.
Data collection/mapping output for exploration surveys.

analysis.innovation_scope_note: Incremental as scored, though genuinely deploying and validating a metal-detection sensor at real ocean depths is a much harder engineering challenge than the score suggests.
analysis.invention_effort_note: Low as scored, but this significantly understates real difficulty, deep-ocean deployment (pressure resistance, waterproofing, real signal transmission from depth) is genuinely hard hardware engineering.

competitive_landscape.note: Highly specialized deep-ocean hardware PS, essentially no hackathon team will have access to real deep-ocean testing conditions.

innovation.note: Metal detection sensing itself is established technology, applied to a genuinely challenging deployment context.

invention.tag: Low on paper, Genuinely Hard in reality
invention.note: The scoring understates the real difficulty of deep-ocean-pressure-resistant hardware deployment and signal transmission.

technical_feasibility.tag: Not Achievable for Real Deep-Ocean Deployment
technical_feasibility.note: There's no hackathon-accessible way to test real deployment at meaningful ocean depths (pressure resistance, waterproofing, communication from depth), this must be scoped to a surface/shallow-water proof-of-concept or a design proposal.

impact_and_benefits.note: Genuine value for a specific deep-ocean mineral exploration context, narrow audience.

architecture.note: This is fundamentally a specialized marine engineering challenge, not a systems-integration task.

overall_verdict.reasoning: Red. Real deep-ocean deployment and validation is not achievable at a hackathon, pressure resistance and communication from real depth require specialized marine engineering testing facilities. A responsible attempt scopes to a shallow-water/surface proof-of-concept of the detection principle, or a design proposal with engineering analysis, not a claimed deep-ocean-ready system.

evaluator_lens.biggest_strength: Very well-specified target deposit types give clear, researchable detection targets even for a scoped-down proof-of-concept.
evaluator_lens.biggest_risk: Any claim of validated deep-ocean deployment capability without real pressure-testing facilities would be a significant overclaim.
evaluator_lens.validate_before_commit: Scope explicitly to demonstrating the metal-detection sensing principle in a shallow-water or surface test setup, and present deep-ocean deployment engineering (pressure housing, communication) as a design proposal, not a validated capability.

idea_0_4: Scope to a shallow-water/surface proof-of-concept of the metal-detection sensing principle (e.g. a basic magnetometer or induction sensor detecting metal samples in a water tank), not real deep-ocean deployment.
Research real deep-ocean deployment engineering requirements (pressure housing design, acoustic/tethered communication) for your design-proposal component.
Split: one person on the detection sensor prototype, one on the deep-deployment design proposal/analysis.
prototype_4_22: Build your detection sensor prototype and test it against real metal samples in a shallow water or surface setup.
Research and draft your deep-ocean deployment engineering proposal (pressure resistance approach, communication method).
Start basic data-logging/mapping output from your sensor tests.
integration_22_30: Test your sensor prototype's detection capability against different simulated metal-deposit types (varying material, size, depth in your test setup).
Compile your deep-deployment design proposal with engineering justification.
Prepare honest documentation of the gap between your proof-of-concept and full deep-ocean readiness.
polish_30_36: Prepare your real detection test results as your core evidence.
Rehearse being explicit about the proof-of-concept versus full-deployment distinction throughout your pitch.
Prepare to discuss what real deep-ocean validation would require.
build_plan.how_to_stand_out: Show your sensor genuinely detecting real metal samples in your shallow-water/surface test setup live, real detection evidence, even if not at ocean depth, is far more credible than an unvalidated deep-ocean claim.

strengths: Very well-specified target deposit types give clear research and testing direction.
Low competition given the genuine deployment difficulty.
weaknesses: No hackathon-achievable path to real deep-ocean deployment validation.
Requires both hardware engineering and marine-science domain knowledge together.

team_fit.ideal_ratio: Hardware-heavy, with dedicated research time for the deep-deployment engineering proposal.
team_fit.approach: Confirm access to a basic sensor (magnetometer or metal detector coil) and a water-test setup before committing to this PS.

ai_buildability_split.needs_human_judgment: The actual sensor engineering and deep-ocean deployment design, that's applied marine/electrical engineering, not something AI tooling designs for you.
ai_buildability_split.risk_of_leaning_on_ai_only: An AI-suggested deep-ocean deployment design without real pressure-engineering validation risks being fundamentally unworkable at actual ocean depths, this needs real engineering rigor.

data_resource_availability.status: No dataset dependency, resourcing risk is physical materials and access to test conditions (even shallow water testing requires planning).
data_resource_availability.backup_plan: If water testing isn't feasible, demonstrate detection capability in a dry setup with metal samples at varying distances, honestly framed as a preliminary sensing demonstration.

judge_qna.question: Did you test this at anything close to real ocean depth?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Be direct: no, real deep-ocean pressure testing requires specialized facilities far beyond hackathon access, we validated the core detection principle in a shallow-water/surface setup and developed an engineering proposal for deep-deployment.
judge_qna.follow_up: What pressure rating would the deployment housing need for the target deposit depths, and how did you determine that?

judge_qna.question: How does your sensor distinguish between different types of metal-rich deposits (nodules versus sulphides versus crusts)?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Describe your detection approach's actual discriminating capability based on your real tests, and be honest about the limits, different deposit types may have different detection signatures that would need further sensor development to fully distinguish.
judge_qna.follow_up: What additional sensing modality would improve deposit-type discrimination?
